messages.subject: Re: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.subject_clean: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.body_plain:
I haven't used `MplusAutomate()` in awhile but very pleased to see this new feature.  Thanks you!!

On Saturday, May 20, 2017 at 9:28:48 AM UTC-4, michael.hallquist wrote:
> Dear MplusAutomation users,
>
> I wanted to give you the update that I've written an initial parser for MODEL INDIRECT output and added it to the development version of the package: https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation. If you have MODEL INDIRECT output, it will be returned in $indirect by readModels(). I haven't tested this extensively, but it works for a file I have that has extensive output of this sort. There are a number of ways I could have formatted the Mplus output into R objects, so please let me know if you have problems with this new parser or suggestions for another way to parse it. At the moment, two data.frames $overall and $specific are the subelements of $indirect, the first containing total, total indirect, and direct effects; the second containing all specific paths with the mediating variables pasted together in the $intervening column.
>
> Hope this helps in your work. This will be part of the forthcoming 0.7 version of the package on CRAN -- that will support Mplus v8, too. Stay tuned...
>
> Best,
> Michael
>
> On Wednesday, February 22, 2017 at 5:01:54 PM UTC-5, michael.hallquist wrote:
> > Hi Catherine,
> >
> > For now the main way to get such details is through explicitly specifying a constraint using MODEL constraint syntax. I've recently asked a student in my lab to help with this section, so with luck, perhaps she will implement this feature in the package.
> >
> > Michael
> >
> > On Monday, January 16, 2017 at 11:50:32 AM UTC-5, Catherine Demers wrote:
> > >
> > > Hi Michael,
> > > I was curious as to whether there have been any updates on extracting parameters from the MODEL INDIRECT section. I have found your package extraordinarily helpful thus far and would love to be able to get these additional parameters.
> > >
> > > best,
> > > Catherine
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, December 11, 2013 at 3:05:04 PM UTC-6, michael.hallquist wrote:
> > > > Hi Markus,
> > > >
> > > > Unfortunately, I have not had time to work on the MODEL INDIRECT section, despite my aspiration. I would be grateful if you could take on programming a parser for this section. Feel free to fork off of our Github and let me know if I can help along the way.
> > > >
> > > > Best,
> > > > Michael
> > > >
> > > > On Tuesday, November 5, 2013 5:21:55 PM UTC-5, mriek wrote:
> > > > > Hi Michael,
> > > > >
> > > > > I would also like to read the MODEL INDIRECT section of the Mplus output to R and I can do some programming work for that. I had a look at your functions to parse other sections and I think I got the main idea of how you are doing it. Anyways, it would be nice if you could tell me where in the dev process you are to avoid double work and pitfalls ;-)
> > > > >
> > > > > Just let me know
> > > > >
> > > > > Best,
> > > > > Markus
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > Am Donnerstag, 18. Juli 2013 11:57:36 UTC-5 schrieb michael.hallquist:
> > > > > > Hi Cathy,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > At this point, the package does not read the output of MODEL INDIRECT, so the total, direct, and indirect effects sections are not available in R. Others have asked for this feature, too, and it's on my "to do" list. The problem is that this section is pretty variable in its format, which makes it hard to parse, but I have worked on it a bit. With luck, this feature will come out in late summer. Other contributors to this effort are welcome, if you're interested.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > Michael
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Tuesday, July 16, 2013 6:33:48 PM UTC-4, Cathy Antonakos wrote:
> > > > > > > This is a great program! I am using Mplus to test indirect effects in many path models, and just used Mplus Automation for the first time this week!
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Is it possible to save the estimates from the total, direct, and indirect effects section of the output? I can obtain the parameter estimates from the OLS and probit regressions. But I'd especially like to obtain the estimates of the indirect effects.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Thanks.
> > > > > > > Cathy

Sookyoung Son,
